Multi-currency account and Currency exchange - Proof of concept for transition to microservice

Draft · proof of concept for the transition to microservices

This is draft document to enable Currency exchange feature by integration with 3rd party. 3rd party can be any SaaS solution that enables Currency exchange (e.g. CurrencyCloud, Wise,…) or FX Liquidity pool (e.g. SuissQuote, …).

The feature will be implemented as Proof of Concept for transformation to Microservice architecture.

The following functionalities should be supported:

  • Multicurrency Account setup
  • Currency exchange (for business and private users)
  • Inward FX remittance - (out of MVP scope)
  • Outward FX remittance - (out of MVP scope)
  • Inward SWIFT transfer - (out of MVP scope)
  • Outward SWIFT transfer - (out of MVP scope)
  • Spending in multiple currencies (e.g. with Debit Card) - (out of MVP scope)
  • Booking
  • Monitoring & Closing Open position
  • Settlement
  • Reconcilliation
  • FX revaluation
  • AML

Currency exchange scenarios allowed (for business and private users)

The following scenarios are allowed (for private and business users):

  • Currency exchange when the same client is owner of both accounts (sender and receiver)
  • Currency exchange enabled Internal Transfer between two OneFor users when:
  • the sender and the receiver are within the same OneFor entity (intra-entity transfer)
  • the receiver is within another OneFor entity (inter-entity transfer).
  • Currency exchange enabled External Bank transfer
  • Client Initiates Transfer from Non-EUR Currency account e.g. send USD to recipient in EUR (only EUR SEPA transfer will be allowed!!!).

Use case scenarios / User stories

1. Multi-currency Account setup

As a system I should enable to setup multicurrency account in the system.

As a Client I would like to have possibility to:

  • Open Multi-Currency Accounts
  • Client uses ONEFOR platform to open wallets in EUR, USD, GBP, CHF.
  • Retrieve balances in all currencies
  • Top-up Accounts in all currencies
  • USD, GBP, CHF accounts can be funded by:
  • Currency exchange (from other currency account of the same customer)
  • Internal Fund Transfer (e.g., internal inter or intra-entity FX transaction)

2. Currency exchange between two currencies of the same customer

As a Client (both Private and Business) I would like to have possibility to exchange money between two currencies of my account:

  • Client Initiates Currency Exchange
  • E.g., Convert EUR 1,000 to USD.
  • FX Rate Provided
  • System retrieves real-time FX rate (e.g 1,12) and applies margin (e.g. 2%).
  • Client Confirms FX Transaction
  • System deducts EUR and credits USD account accordingly.
  • Margin fee is booked on P&L accounts accordingly.
  • Conversion Executed Internally
  • Ledger microservice updates both accounts and GL accounts instantly.
  • Treasury microservice monitors Open position and triggers rebalancing if needed (at End of Day or once treshold is reached).

3. Currency exchange enabled Internal transfers

As a Client (both private and business) I would like to have possibility to send money in another currency (making currency exchange during transfer) to another OneFor client within the same entity or between two entities:

  • Sender Initiates Currency Exchange Internal Transfer
  • E.g., Convert EUR 1,000 to USD
  • Insert data about Receiver acoount
  • FX Rate Provided
  • System retrieves real-time FX rate (e.g 1,12) and applies margin (e.g. 2%).
  • Sender confirms FX Transaction
  • System deducts EUR and credits USD account accordingly.
  • Margin fee is booked on P&L accounts accordingly.
  • Conversion Executed Internally
  • Ledger microservice updates both accounts and GL accounts instantly.
  • Treasury microservice monitors Open position and triggers rebalancing if needed (at End of Day or once treshold is reached).

4. Currency exchange enabled External Bank transfer

As a Client (both private and business) I would like to have possibility to make SEPA transfer by sending EUR (making currency exchange during transfer) to IBAN account.

  • Client Initiates Transfer from Non-EUR Currency account
  • E.g. Send USD to recipient in EUR (only EUR SEPA transfer will be allowed!!!).
  • Sender Initiates Currency Exchange
  • E.g., Convert 1,130 USD to 1,000 EUR
  • Insert data about Receiver IBAN
  • FX Rate Provided
  • System retrieves real-time FX rate (e.g 1,12) and applies margin (e.g. 2%).
  • Sender confirms FX Transaction
  • System reserved balance on USD account accordingly.
  • SEPA Credit Transfer confirmation received
  • Once confirmation that SEPA transfer is executed (either by Moorwand for EU or by BPB for Kosovo), System released reserved balance on USD account.
  • System book Debit Sender account and Credit Nostro account.

5. Currency exchange - booking

As a system I should enable the following accounting/booking features in Core Banking system.

This is the basic scenario when both accounts are within the same entity. Business will confirm.

Transaction 1 (Client exchange €1.000 to USD):

  • Market rate EUR/USD: 1.20 = Buy or Bid rate - Market rate is taken from Currency exchange or liquidity pool provider
  • Margin fee 2%: 1.000 × 0.02 = 20 EUR - Margin fee is always taken from sold ccy in currency pair
  • USD to client: 980 × 1.2 = 1.176,00 USD

Transaction 2 (Client exchange €2.000 to USD):

  • Market rate EUR/USD: 1.19 = Buy or Bid rate Market rate is taken from Currency exchange or liquidity pool provider
  • Margin fee 2%: 2.000 × 0.02 = 40 EUR - Margin fee is always taken from sold ccy in currency pair
  • USD to client: 1.960 × 1.19 = 2.332,40 USD

Transaction 3 (Client exchange 2.500USD to EUR):

  • Market rate USD/EUR: 1.18 = Sell or Ask rate Market rate is taken from Currency exchange or liquidity pool provider
  • Margin fee 2%: 2.500 × 0.02 = 50 USD (at the end of day we will convert it in Domestic currency)
  • EUR to client: 2.450 (1/1.18) = 2.076,27 EUR

Transaction 4 (Client exchange 500GBP to CHF):

  • Market rate GBP/CHF: 1.11 = Buy or Bid rate Market rate is taken from Currency exchange or liquidity pool provider
  • Margin fee 2%: 500 × 0.02 = 10 GBP (at the end of day we will convert it in Domestic currency)
  • CHF to client: 490 x 1.11 = 543.9 CHF

6. Open position

As a Treasury back-office user I would like to have constant real-time monitoring of Open position (all balances in non-domestic currency).

E.g. in countries like North Macedonia or Albania where EUR is not local currency, all balances in EUR accounts (loans, deposits, accounts, GL account) should be monitored as open position.

We have two approaches to monitor open position:

a) monitor Open position per Currency pair (usually Treasury middle-office monitor FX deals on that way). It is easier to compute mark-to-market (MTM) valuations, to calculate realized/unrealized P&L and execute trades within the same currency pair to close open position and eliminate currency risk.

b) monitor Open position per Currency is used to monitor overall Bank exposure in case You offer more foreign currency products (loans, deposits, …) and for FX revaluation and General ledger purposes.

This will be discussed, but usually combined approaches should be used.

Monitoring Break even price for currency pair:

Break even price should be monitored comparing to the current market rate (match-to-market). Break even price is calculated for currency pair.

Screens what will present the all FX deals (FX blotter) and screens what will monitor the following values for selected currency pair (e.g. EUR/USD) should be designed:

Total EUR long (bought): 2.076,27 EUR

Total EUR short (sold): 2.940 EUR (amount without margin fee because the fee is already booked)

Net EUR: -863,73 EUR (short)

Total USD long (bought): 3.508,4 USD

Total EUR short (sold): 2.450 USD (amount without margin fee because the fee is already booked)

Net USD: +1.058,4 USD (long)

Break even price = Total quoted currency including fee (USD) / Total base currency including fee (EUR) = 1.008,4 / 923,73 = 1,09166

Adjusted Break even price = Total quoted currency (USD) / Total base currency (EUR) = 1.058,4 / 863,73 = 1,225383

This case would like to tell us that:

Below 1,091661 - we are in profit.

Between 1,091661 - 1,225383 - we will book realised loss but we are still compensated with Margin fee that is booked and Total gain is positive.

Above 1,225383 - we have to book realized loss that is higher than gain margin fee.

1.0916611008.4923.730.0045.8060105.80In-the-money
1.151008.4876.87-46.8643.486056.62In-the-money
1.2253831008.4822.93-100.8040.80600.00At-the-money
1.281008.4787.81-135.9239.0660-36.86Out-of-the-money

Alerting can be settled up that in case of reaching At-the-money position, we initiate immediate trade/closing position. In that case we will be protected on higher exchange rate (for particular currency pair) fluctuation during date.

Of course, higher margin fee protect us better and we are resillient for higher daily calculation.

Typical daily volatility ~0.7%
2%+ moves Extreme and rare
Est. occurrences in 20 years Likely under 20

6.b) Monitoring Open position per currency / Net currency exposure

As a Treasury back-office user I would like to have constant real-time monitoring of Open position per currency pair.

Net currency exposure refers to overall exposure to a single currency across all transactions and all accounts — aggregated by currency. It sums up all bought positions minus sold positions (from FX deals) plus foreign currency customer account balances (loans, deposits) plus GL account balances (e.g. P&L accounts) in that currency.

See how it should look like after 4 transaction:

Limits are tightly connected with exposures. Separate limits can be settled up for each currency on FX trading, Credit lines, Deposits etc. Overall exposure could be or could not be sum of them.

Alerting can be settled up for automatic closing position if we breach exposure limit for particular product in particular currency.

Local currency (in our case EUR) is not considered as Currency risk exposure.

7. Settlement

There will not be classical settlement. Settlement will be done by Closing Open position. To be confirmed with provider.

8. Reconcilliation

As a back-office user I would like to reconcile/compare the list of tranmsactions on Currency Exchange provider side and OneFor list of FX transactions. Reconcilliation of transaction to be confirmed with provider.

The important things what should be considered for Reconciliation.

Closing position will usually happen at the end of working time (e.g. 17h) what means that reconcile period will cover 2 days (e.g. from 17:00 June 7th - 17:00 June 8th).

Additionally, when we close position we have to mark (change status) for all deals that are covered with closing deal. E.g. closing deal can be executed every day at 17:00, but covering all deals that are executed till 16:00.

9. FX revaluation

As a back-office user I want to make FX revaluation of all opened positions in foreign currency for GL accounting and reporting purposes.

This is regular General ledger process that could be applied to any open position in foreign currency (Loans, Deposits, …) and it is not strictly related to FX transaction. General solution for FX Revaluation process should be agreed, it can be either part of Accounting/GL microservice or can be executed in SAP.

Assuming that Current Account balances in foreign currency are safeguarded, they should not be Revaluated at the end of day. According to the above mentioned examples the only opened position in whole FX process will remain P&L Margin fee in sold currency. We can either a) keep it in foreign currency and make FX revaluation for reporting purposes or b) exchange it to local currency (for Kosovo and EU entity it is EUR).

11. FX hedging

There are different options usually used for hedging of FX transactions. Some of usually used are the following, but no one of them seems as more propriate to hedge the risk of intra-day Currency exchange rate fluctuation. Business to confirm.

Cash FX transactions - transaction with same business day/value today - easiest way of protecting. Can be done as contra transaction for each FX deal or as settlement at the end of day (we are still exposed to intra-day currency exchange risk).

Tom FX transactions - with settlment T+1

Spot FX Transactions - with settlement T+2

FX forward - a contract to buy or sell a currency at a specified rate on a future date (e.g. next day, 1 week)

FX Swaps - a combination of a cash/tom/spot FX transaction and a simultaneous forward transaction

FX futures - standardized contracts traded on regulated exchanges, obligating parties to buy or sell currencies at set prices and dates

FX option - a contract that grant the buyer the right—but not the obligation—to exchange currency at a specified exchange rate before or on the option’s expiration date

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) - Forward contracts settled in cash rather than physical delivery of currencies, especially used for restricted or non-convertible currencies

Structured FX Products - Customized derivative instruments combining elements like forwards, options, and swaps to create tailored risk management solutions

If needed this will be contracted separately with provider. Example of the provided hedging service You can find here

Glossary

FX - stands for Foreign currency Exchange.

FX Remittance - refers to the transfer of funds across borders, involving currency conversion. Can be outward and inward (outgoing and incoming).

Swift Transfer - refers to electronic money transfers between two bank accounts globally using SWIFT (Society for Worldwide Interbank Financial Telecommunications) network. Can be outward and inward (outgoing and incoming) and optinally can include currency conversion.

External transfer - refers to Transfer when sender is OneFor client and receiver is not OneFor client.

Internal transfer - refers to Transfer when both, senderand receiver, are OneFor clients. Can be inter-entity (between two different OneFor entities e.g. Kosovo and Europe) and intra-entity (between two clients within the same OneFor entiy.

Base Currency -This is the first currency listed in a currency pair. In the pair EUR/USD, the euro (EUR) is the base currency.

Quoted Currency - This is the second currency in the pair. In the EUR/USD example, the US dollar (USD) is the quoted currency.

Break-Even Price - is the currency exchange rate at which the net position’s mark-to-market (MTM) value would be zero (i.e., no profit or loss).

At-the-Money (ATM) - The current market rate equals the break-even rate (no profit or loss).

In-the-Money (OTM) - The current market rate is favorable compared to our break-even — i.e., the position would result in a profit if closed immediately.

Out-of-the-Money (OTM) - The current market rate is unfavorable compared to our break-even — i.e., the position would result in a loss if closed immediately.

Long position - Taking long position means that we are buying (having possesion) on some asset. If we buy 1.100 USD for 1.000 EUR we are going long on USD (we buy it) and short in EUR (we are selling it). Or it can be used that we are going long in EUR/USD currency pair.

Short position - Taking short position means that we are selling (not having possesion) on some asset. If we buy 1.100 USD for 1.000 EUR we are going long on USD (we buy it) and short in EUR (we are selling it).
